messages:
nora: Heads-up: after rolling BMC v2.4.1 to eu2-rack-3 we saw ~22 nodes report OOB PHY down while host NIC stays up. Autoscaler pulled GPUs. Sample log:
```
[eu2-r3-07] bmc: phy_train_fail retries=4 state=0x7
[eu2-r3-19] bmc: nvram_write OK but checksum_diff=0x2
```
Is this the keystore migration touching nvram?

devin: Yep, migration ran during the window. Prom shows `bmc_nvram_write_errors` and `oob_phy_fail` spike at 01:12 UTC. Most affected have Avago SFPs but a few are Aquantia.

oscar: Quick triage: try soft BMC reset first (`bmc reset soft`) and avoid toggling secureboot. If soft reset fails, do an NVRAM restore from snapshot.

maya: I've paused the rollout for other eu2 racks. I'll gather `ethtool -m` dumps and SFP vendor/rev. Also flagged cost: autoscaler spun replacements in us-west, temporary cost ~ $1.5k/hr. Finance looped.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-4712 created: "eu2-rack-3: BMC NVRAM checksum diffs -> OOB PHY failures". Paging oncall.

devin: Soft reset on eu2-r3-07 recovered link in ~22s. eu2-r3-19 didn't recover; NVRAM restore succeeded on -19 and link came back. Restores failing on 3 hosts with older SFP rev strings.

oscar: Plan:
1) Keep rollout paused (maya)
2) Canary NVRAM restore on 6 nodes (devin/oscar)
3) If >75% success, rollback migration for remaining nodes in rack-3 and add SFP-rev whitelist to migration script
4) If not, schedule ToR port-bounces and vendor microcode update window
Who can patch the migration script?

maya: I'll own the script patch and add preflight that checks `sfp_vendor_rev` and aborts on unknown revs. Will also add an abort threshold: >10% nvram checksum diffs -> stop rollout.

devin: Good. Also add alerting for `bmc_nvram_checksum_diff_ratio` and a dashboard tile for SFP vendor distribution per rack.

oscar: I'll coordinate vendor microcode drops for affected revs. We should also add a canary that does a soft-reset + ethtool verify post-migration for two vendor types before continuing.

nora: Thanks. I'll collect list of affected hosts and start the post-incident doc once we confirm root cause (migration vs SFP rev incompatibility).
